purpose: restore service quickly and safely when something is broken, with clear command and communication
entry_criteria: An alert or report indicates user impact
Severity levels and roles are defined
procedure: Acknowledge, assign an incident commander and open a single incident channel and record.
Classify severity by user impact and blast radius; escalate per severity.
Check recent changes and dashboards; choose the safest mitigation (rollback, feature flag, failover) before searching for root cause.
Communicate status at a fixed interval to stakeholders and affected users.
Verify recovery with user-facing checks and metrics, then close or downgrade.
Hand off timeline and artifacts to the postmortem (stage 165).
acceptance_criteria: Single commander and channel were named
Customer-impact communications were sent on schedule
Recovery was verified by metrics, not by absence of alerts
Timeline is complete enough for a postmortem
validation_method: Recovery verified by an independent check.

validation.check: compare error rate and latency to pre-incident baseline for 30 minutes

validation.expect: changes before the incident are listed in the record

failure_modes.detection: No status update inside the interval

worked_example: ILLUSTRATIVE: Error rate jumps right after a release. The commander rolls back within ten minutes, confirms the error rate returns to baseline, and keeps the incident open for thirty minutes of observation.
